$comment: Documented differences between Copilot Studio harnesses, by concept. Each record explains one concept on each harness, so a lab written for one harness can offer an expandable 'How this differs on the <other> harness' block. Everything here is grounded on Microsoft Learn pages listed in `sources`; nothing is invented. `availability` is one of supported, preview, planned, not-supported, or unknown, and is set from what the page says: 'supported' reflects a Learn comparison table, and 'preview' only where a page labels the feature preview. A harness whose behavior Learn does not describe is marked `unknown`, and a record that leans on that carries `confidence: uncertain` or `partly-documented` with an `uncertainNote`, which the lab shows as 'Not confirmed in Microsoft Learn'. Use the exact name 'Microsoft Copilot harness' and US English. Re-verify a record by re-reading `verifiedAgainst`; update `lastVerified` only after doing so.

standard.summary: Best for rule-based agents and structured conversations where you define the topics and paths and want consistent, predictable answers. Complex scenarios can need extensive custom routing and exception logic.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Best for long-running, multi-step business processes: it takes a goal, breaks it into steps, and adjusts when a step fails. Simple scenarios can incur extra reasoning, latency, and Copilot Credit consumption without a better result.
limits: Validate that the channels and features you need are available as the experience matures.

customer-conversation.summary: Best for customer-facing agents over voice and chat, with specialized subagents and escalation to a human representative.

standard.summary: Agents built with the Standard harness remain fully supported alongside agents on the other harnesses.

microsoft-copilot.summary: You choose the harness when you create the agent. You describe the agent in natural language (preview) and the system generates the underlying configuration, then you refine it on the Build tab.
microsoft-copilot.where: Copilot Studio home page, then create a new agent powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.
limits: An agent created with the Microsoft Copilot harness can't be transferred to the Standard harness. Copilot Studio can create a Microsoft Copilot harness agent from a Standard agent.

customer-conversation.summary: Describe the agent in natural language to generate a starting primary agent, or start from a blank agent.
customer-conversation.where: Copilot Studio home page or the Agents tab.

standard.summary: Instructions guide the agent, and explicit topics, triggers, and branching conversation flows also shape its behavior.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Instructions define the agent's identity, tone, scope, and behavior, and they carry more of the load because you describe the agent in natural language instead of authoring topic flows. Response language is controlled by the instructions.

customer-conversation.summary: Only the primary agent's instructions can include modality-specific guidance, separated into Speech and Chat tabs.

standard.summary: You can configure orchestration behavior. Some advanced models and newer agentic capabilities aren't available.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Every agent uses the enhanced orchestration model, so there is no orchestration mode to switch. Reasoning models and some emerging agentic capabilities are available only through this harness. You choose the model from the Build tab.

customer-conversation.summary: Uses a multi-agent architecture with specialized subagents, each able to escalate to a human representative.

standard.summary: Supports public websites, file upload, SharePoint, Graph connectors, Dataverse tables, and Azure AI Search.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Supports public websites, file upload, SharePoint, Graph connectors, and Dataverse tables. Memory adds context from earlier interactions.
limits: Azure AI Search isn't supported as a knowledge source.

customer-conversation.summary: Connected data sources ground the agent's responses. Speech channels don't support end-user sign-in, so knowledge sources that require end-user credentials only work for Chat conversations.

standard.summary: Connectors, MCP, workflows, prompt tools, and the computer use tool are supported.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Connectors, MCP, and workflows are supported. Tools let the agent perform actions such as calling APIs and running flows.
limits: Computer use is planned, not yet supported.
Prompt tools are not supported. Skills replace them.

customer-conversation.summary: Calls tools across connectors, knowledge, MCP, and connected agents, plus prebuilt contact-center tools such as Escalate and Biometric Authentication.

standard.summary: AI prompts (prompt tools) are supported as a tool type. Skills are not supported on the Standard harness.

microsoft-copilot.summary: A skill is a name, a description, and Markdown instructions that you create from blank, generate with AI, or upload as a file or package. The orchestration runtime invokes a skill when a request matches its description. Skills replace prompt tools and can be shared across agents. The harness also provides built-in skills for analyzing CSV, Word, HTML, Markdown, PDF, PowerPoint, and Excel files.
microsoft-copilot.where: Build tab, then add a skill.

customer-conversation.summary: Supports two skill types: Generative skills (instructions-based, like Microsoft Copilot harness skills) and Topic skills (deterministic authored flows that match the Topics concept).

standard.summary: Connect to an MCP server and its tools and resources through the agent's tools.

microsoft-copilot.summary: MCP is supported as a tool type. You can also publish the agent itself to MCP and A2A clients through the MCP client and A2A client channels, which are in preview.

customer-conversation.summary: The harness can call tools across connectors, knowledge, MCP, and connected agents.

standard.summary: Supports connected Copilot Studio agents in the same environment, Foundry agents, A2A protocol agents, and Microsoft 365 SDK agents. Context is distributed across topics, variables, tools, and subagents, so makers manage the handoffs.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Supports the same connected agent types. The orchestrator keeps unified context as work flows back from connected agents, and subagent conversations can continue with shared context.

customer-conversation.summary: A sub-agent shares configuration, deployment, and ALM with its primary agent. A connected agent, such as an agent hosted in Azure AI Foundry, keeps independent configuration and ALM so it can be reused across orchestrations.

differences.title: SDK and extensibility
differences.uncertainNote: The pages reviewed for this lab do not describe how the Microsoft Agents SDK, the web chat SDK, or editor-based authoring differ between harnesses. The only documented point is that Microsoft 365 SDK agents can be connected agents on both the Standard and Microsoft Copilot harnesses. Check the harness comparison page before you rely on any other SDK behavior.

standard.summary: A Microsoft 365 SDK agent can be added as a connected agent.

microsoft-copilot.summary: A Microsoft 365 SDK agent can be added as a connected agent. Other SDK behavior is not confirmed.

customer-conversation.summary: Not described on the pages reviewed.

standard.summary: Memory is not supported on the Standard harness. Context lives in topics and variables.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Turn Memory on for an agent and it keeps a separate, private memory for each user: it captures signals such as preferences, stores them as files in Microsoft-managed storage, and applies them in later conversations. Users review or delete memories in chat or in the memory portal; makers can't view them.
limits: Memories are deleted after 28 days without interaction.
User memory is disabled in group chats and Microsoft Teams channels.
Turning Memory off doesn't delete stored memories.

customer-conversation.summary: Has a separate, structured Memory capability with its own retention period and configuration.

differences.title: Files and code execution
differences.uncertainNote: Learn's comparison says working with files is not a focus of the Customer Conversation or Standard harnesses, but it does not say whether either one blocks it.

standard.summary: Code interpreter is an opt-in capability. Creating and editing files isn't a focus of this harness.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Natively creates, edits, and reasons over Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files. Code interpreter is native, and each task runs in a secure sandbox governed by Copilot Studio.

customer-conversation.summary: Working with files isn't a focus of this harness according to the comparison page.

standard.summary: You author topics, triggers, and branching conversation flows, and the agent follows the paths you define. Custom entities and manual authentication are available.

microsoft-copilot.summary: You describe behavior in natural language and the harness reasons through it instead of following authored topic flows. Hooks replace topic triggers for lifecycle moments.

customer-conversation.summary: Topic skills are deterministic authored flows that match the Topics concept, and Events turn built-in responses such as Conversation Start, End of Conversation, and On Error on or off.

standard.summary: Triggers on user intent and other system triggers, such as Message received, are handled by topics.

microsoft-copilot.summary: A hook runs one of your workflows every time a lifecycle event fires: Start, User prompt submitted, Error, Pre tool use, Post tool use, or After tool failure. Pre tool use is the only event that can block an action. You configure hooks from the agent's command bar, not the Build tab.
microsoft-copilot.where: Top menu bar, three dots (...), then Hooks.
limits: A hook that fails, times out, or returns something unreadable doesn't stop the agent, so don't make it your only safeguard.
The workflow must be published, and a hook doesn't run for users until you publish the agent.

customer-conversation.summary: Events turn built-in responses for common conversation moments on or off, such as Conversation Start, End of Conversation, and On Error.

standard.summary: Workflows are supported as a tool, and the harness is suited to structured, repeatable workflows.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Workflows are supported as a tool and give predictable, deterministic steps while the agent reasons through the rest. The same workflow can also be bound to a hook.

standard.summary: Supports Microsoft 365 and Teams, websites, SharePoint, WhatsApp, and Dynamics 365 Contact Center, among others.

microsoft-copilot.summary: Publish to Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, a demo website, or a web app, to internal teams or external customers. The MCP client and A2A client channels are in preview and available only in early release cycle environments.
